title: Google Rejiggers TPU Accelerators For Broader AI Inference Work
gist: Google is rolling out modified Sunfish TPU 8t and Zebrafish TPU 8i variants (TPU 8tx and 8i Max) in 2027, tuned for agentic and large-context inference. The author also covers the TPU 8tx switch to an AMD Epyc host, 8i Max's HBM tradeoffs, and TPU Sync memory software.

insights.claim: Google's TPU 8t Sunfish is made via Broadcom and is expected to be rolling into Google datacenters now, while the MediaTek-shepherded TPU 8i Zebrafish had delays earlier this year and its shipment status to Google is unclear.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Dual-vendor custom silicon sourcing spreads Google TPU design wins to Broadcom and MediaTek.
insights.locator: To be specific, there are two new variants

insights.claim: The modified Sunfish and Zebrafish systems are expected in 2027, with the author optimistically predicting Q1 2027 and a ramp over the next year and a half to multiple Google Cloud regions.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan

insights.claim: Ironwood TPU v7p, deployed internally in Q4 2025, took roughly a year before enough excess capacity existed to rent on Google Cloud, with pricing now listed in US-Central1 and Europe-West2.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Google keeps new TPUs for internal use first, delaying external availability.
insights.locator: For instance, in the interim between the Sunfish and Zebrafish

insights.claim: TPU 8t is designed for training, with a 3D torus interconnect spanning 9,600 accelerators in a shared coherent memory space and 121 exaflops at FP4.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Largest shared-memory AI footprint supports Google's frontier training lead.
insights.locator: The TPU 8t was explicitly designed to run AI training workloads

insights.claim: Google organizes 9,600-unit pods into clusters of over 1 million TPU 8t devices, and said such a cluster trained Gemini 4 Carbon, announced October 28 after delays.
insights.speaker: Mark Lohmeyer
insights.so_what: Million-chip training clusters show scale of Google's in-house compute.
insights.locator: On a conference call going over the new TPU machines

insights.claim: Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon have introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input at 95 percent off.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Token pricing benchmarks the cost of frontier inference.
insights.locator: For API access through Google Cloud

insights.claim: TPU 8tx replaces the 3D torus with the boardfly (dragonfly variant) interconnect, shrinking pods from 9,600 to 1,152 accelerators, with an 8.3x smaller fabric diameter and about half the average latency, to suit agentic inference with many concurrent streams.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Interconnect topology is being specialised for inference rather than training.
insights.locator: The TPU 8tx is a special variant

insights.claim: TPU 8tx swaps Google's Axion Arm CPU for an unnamed AMD Epyc because AMD's on-board root of trust and encryption accelerators keep workloads encrypted until used on the TPUs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A confidential-computing win for AMD in a Google AI system.
insights.locator: The other change with the TPU 8tx

insights.claim: The author bets the TPU 9 family and next-generation Axion CPUs will embed the security functions, making the AMD win a short-term victory.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AMD's share of Google TPU hosts may not last.
insights.quote: I would bet that with the TPU 9 family and the next-generation Axion CPUs it will be
insights.locator: Google has its own encryption and security processors

insights.claim: TPU 8i Max doubles Zebrafish chips per socket but HBM capacity per socket is up only 33 percent, because each chip drops from 288 GB to 192 GB (same 8.6 TB/sec per chip), implying a move from twelve-high to eight-high HBM3 stacks.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Less HBM per unit of compute may strand compute, but it targets larger context and KV cache footprints.
insights.locator: With the TPU 8i Max, Google is focusing on larger context

insights.claim: The author argues Google is spreading HBM3 over more chips and tightly coupling two Zebrafish chips for a bigger shared memory pool for context and KV cache, accepting possibly stranded compute over insufficient memory.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Memory capacity, not compute, constrains long-context inference economics.
insights.quote: This could leave some compute stranded, but that is not as bad as not having enough memory per socket to run large context.
insights.locator: Everything in architecture is a tradeoff

insights.claim: The author expects training TPUs to carry a premium, with TPU 8t pricier per flops and per HBM capacity than TPU 8i, TPU 8tx a slight premium, and TPU 8i Max a little under 2x TPU 8i per hour; Google has not yet priced them.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Pricing will signal how Google values training versus inference capacity.
insights.locator: It is reasonable to expect for Google to charge a premium

insights.claim: The elasticity of the GenAI market depends on ever-decreasing costs of producing tokens for inference.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Falling per-token cost is the demand driver for inference silicon.
insights.locator: It is reasonable to expect for Google to charge a premium

insights.claim: TPU Sync is a hierarchical storage management software layer that moves an agent's working memory off the TPU when it pauses and restores it on resume, because agentic TPUs are often idle a large percentage of the time.
insights.speaker: Mark Lohmeyer
insights.so_what: Raising utilisation lowers cost per agentic transaction, a key inference economics lever.

insights.claim: TPU Sync is software, so Google has back-cast it to TPU 5, 6, 7 and 8, but it is unclear how it orchestrates memory across huge clusters or how much it boosts throughput.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Throughput benefits are unproven and need data.
insights.quote: It is also not clear how much TPU Sync boosts inference throughput.
insights.locator: And because TPU Sync is software
